title: High-Resolution 3D Visualization of Insect Regenerating Legs via Micro-CT
author: Li, Cheng, et al.

steps.title: Anesthetize nymphal insects with CO₂
steps.instruction: Place the nymphal American cockroach (Periplaneta americana) in a CO₂ chamber and expose to carbon dioxide until fully anesthetized.

steps.title: Excise distal leg segments
steps.instruction: Using Vannas spring scissors (8 cm) under a stereoscopic microscope, cut off the distal tarsus, tibia, and femur of a metathoracic hindleg at the trochanter‑femur junction, preserving the trochanter and coxa for regeneration observation.

steps.title: Incubate for regeneration
steps.instruction: Place the insects in plastic cages at 27 °C with 70 %–80 % relative humidity for approximately 10 days to allow leg regeneration.

steps.title: Prepare fixation and dehydration reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the following solutions: (a) 10 % formalin; (b) 10 % HCl by diluting 35 %–37 % hydrochloric acid with deionized water; (c) 1× PBS by diluting stock 10× PBS ten‑fold with deionized water; (d) Ethanol series of 90 %, 80 %, 70 %, 50 %, and 30 % v/v ethanol in deionized water. When handling acidic solutions, wear gloves and safety glasses. Alternative fixatives such as 4 % formaldehyde or 10 % formalin may be used with appropriate concentration adjustments.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 35 %–37 % HCl to 10 % with deionized water.
Prepare ethanol solutions at 90 %, 80 %, 70 %, 50 %, and 30 % v/v.

steps.title: Verify micro‑CT instrument
steps.instruction: Activate the micro‑CT machine, check that all settings are optimal, and confirm proper functionality before scanning.

steps.title: Complete Amira software training
steps.instruction: Attend basic training sessions to acquire proficiency in operating the Amira visualization software.

steps.title: Collect regenerated leg samples
steps.instruction: Using Vannas spring scissors (8 cm), a stereoscopic microscope, a CO₂ tank, and a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, open the CO₂ tank valve, anesthetize the insects, and excise the regenerated leg portions into the Eppendorf tube.

substeps.instruction: Gather materials: Vannas spring scissors (8 cm), stereoscopic microscope, CO₂ tank, 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Open CO₂ tank valve and anesthetize insects.
Excise regenerated leg tissue and place into the tube.

steps.title: Cut filter paper strips
steps.instruction: Cut filter paper into strips measuring 1.2 cm × 3 cm with scissors.

steps.title: Prepare sample baskets and wash
steps.instruction: Gather adequate sample baskets for the critical point dryer and wash them thoroughly with ethanol.

description: 1.Insect preparation for leg regeneration study.a.Anesthetize the nymphal insects (e.g., American cockroach, Periplaneta americana) using CO2.b.Excise the distal tarsus, tibia, and femur of a metathoracic hindleg at the trochanter-femur junction, preserving the trochanter and coxa for regeneration observation.c.Allow approximately 10 days for nymphs to undergo regeneration at 27°C with a relative humidity of 70%–80% in plastic cages.2.Prepare fixation and dehydration reagents as outlined in the key resources table.3.Ensure proper functionality of the micro-CT apparatus by activating the machine and verifying optimal settings.4.Acquire proficiency in operating the Amira software through basic training sessions.
